waveC.title: Free-form AI, AI privacy, shared comments (others' comments in Activity), in-app reminders
waveC.why: Need the backend (F-2101..F-2103); they go in the backend batches, not a client wave.

rulings: Ask Splito (F-2301) offline-first approach: a deterministic on-device engine in apps/client/src/lib/ask. A keyword/grammar parser (English + Hindi) maps a question to a fixed intent set: balance with a person, who owes me most / whom I owe most, group balance and who owes whom, spend by period/category/group/person, trend by month/day, find expenses (hands to the existing search_terms search), and 'split X N ways' (action card). Answers read only the balances, aggregates and search_terms projections and paged byDate/byGroupDate ranges (§9.8), compute with @splito/domain, show one line per currency, and are labelled 'Answered on this device'. Anything outside the intents gets 'I can answer this once you sign in' plus the closest supported question. Nothing leaves the device. Free-form language needs the backend model (F-2302) and the privacy controls (F-2303); until then there is no AI toggle, no network call and no fake answer.
Ask chat history and draft are device-only (#/storage, capped at 200 messages, 'Clear chat'): not ledger data, never in the database, outbox or backup.

F-2301 acc 1's 'Analytics header right action' is superseded by §26.19 (§26 wins): the Sparkles Search & Ask button already sits in the Analytics header, so there is no second button. B1 corrects the BACKLOG text.

Schema v4 belongs to B5 alone: the `reminders` store plus entity type `reminder`. No other slot edits schema.ts STORES or SCHEMA_VERSION, migrate.ts, the idbStore/sqlStore upgrade code or types.ts EntityType. Comments use the existing v3 `comments` store (byTarget). F-403 tax classes and charges live in the expense `data` JSON, with a read-time adapter for old expenses. Per-merchant charge setups go in a capped account pref (`bill.merchantSetups`). Deleted groups in the bin are read from the small, non-money groups store with no new index. A removed friend is a soft `removedAt` in person data.

Hot shared files take one-line mounts; the logic lives in each slot's own files. Person overflow order: Call it even, [B5 Remind / Remind me], Edit friend, [B6 Export statement], Remove friend (B6 swaps in the guarded flow). Group overflow: Edit group, [B6 Export], Members, Add members, Payment rules, [B3 Archive / Leave / Delete]. Only B2 edits Person/index.tsx outside those mounts (the currency lines).

preferences.ts anchors, so the inserts do not collide: B1 changes MIN_TABS, MAX_TABS and the tabs validator; B2 changes `split.roundTo` and adds `rightColumn.languageDropdown` after `amount.shorthand`; B4 adds `comments.showHistory` after `history.binDays`; B5 adds `notify.*` after `notify.invite`; B7 adds `bill.*` after `categories`.

activity.ts is touched only by B3 (restored kinds, group membership kinds) and B5 (reminder kinds), each as separate union members and case blocks. B4 adds no Activity kind: others' comments arrive with F-2208. New sync mutations go in new modules (groupLifecycle.ts, comments.ts, reminders.ts, backup.ts); mutations.ts is B3's, and B3 keeps the exported signatures of write, requireLive and MutationCtx unchanged.

Routes: B6 adds FriendsAndInvites ('/settings/friends') right after RecentlyDeleted, before SettingsSection, because the first match wins. B4 adds Repayment ('/payment/:repaymentId') after Expense. Each also edits lib/routes/types.ts and navigation/Navigation.tsx at the same relative spot.

Generated and shared docs are fixed at assembly. Builders run lingui extract/compile and fill hi on their own branch. The assembler merges .po entries by msgid (keeping every hi translation), then re-extracts. A pnpm-lock.yaml conflict is resolved by re-running pnpm install after package.json merges (B5 adds expo-notifications; B6 may add expo-print, expo-sharing, expo-document-picker). The assembler alone recounts the BACKLOG status line and Epics table.

PDF statement: native uses expo-print (printToFileAsync, then the share sheet); web opens a print-ready statement and the browser's Save as PDF. Nothing is generated on a server, and there is no PDF library.

F-1907 on the web: browsers cannot schedule notifications while the app is closed, so web reminders fire only while Splito is open, plus an in-app banner on next open. The UI says so. Native fires in airplane mode.
